tries__word-search-ii.title: Word Search II
tries__word-search-ii.pattern: Build a Trie of words, then DFS the board pruning by Trie edges
tries__word-search-ii.statement: Given an `m x n` board of characters and a list of `words`, return all words that can be formed by a sequence of adjacent (up/down/left/right) cells, where each cell is used at most once per word.
constraints: board[i][j] and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Trie + backtracking DFS on the board
approaches.idea: Insert all words into a Trie, storing the full word at its terminal node. Run DFS from every cell, advancing simultaneously through the board and the Trie; prune instantly when the current letter has no matching Trie child. When a node holds a word, collect it and null it out to avoid duplicates. Sharing prefixes across words in the Trie is what makes this far faster than searching each word independently.
approaches.time: O(m*n*4^L) worst case where L is max word length, but heavily pruned by the Trie

tries__word-search-ii.insight: Flip the search: put the dictionary in a Trie and walk the board once, letting Trie edges prune dead branches.

tries__design-add-and-search-words.title: Design Add and Search Words
tries__design-add-and-search-words.statement: Design a data structure that supports `addWord(word)` and `search(word)`, where `search` may contain the wildcard `'.'` that matches any single letter. Return whether any added word matches.
constraints: word in addWord consists of lowercase English letters
word in search consists of '.' or lowercase English letters
At most 10^4 calls to addWord and search

approaches.name: Trie with recursive wildcard search
approaches.idea: Store words in a standard 26-way Trie. Search recursively: a normal letter follows the single matching child, while `'.'` branches into every non-null child and succeeds if any branch matches the remainder. Recursion depth is bounded by word length, so wildcards only fan out where they appear.
approaches.time: O(n) per addWord; per search O(n) with no dots, up to O(26^d * n) with d dots
approaches.space: O(total characters added) plus O(word length) recursion stack

tries__design-add-and-search-words.insight: A '.' in the query means try every child; everything else is an ordinary Trie walk.

tries__maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
tries__maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-.pattern: Binary (bitwise) Trie, greedily pick opposite bits
tries__maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum value of `nums[i] XOR nums[j]` over all pairs `i, j`.

approaches.name: Binary Trie of bits, greedy per bit
approaches.idea: Insert every number into a binary Trie from the most significant bit down. For each number, greedily walk the Trie choosing the opposite bit whenever available, which maximizes that bit of the XOR; if the opposite child is missing, take the same bit. Each query builds the best possible partner one bit at a time, giving the global maximum in O(32) per number.

tries__maximum-xor-of-two-numbers-in-an-.insight: Store numbers as bit-paths in a binary Trie and greedily chase the opposite bit at each level.

tries__maximum-xor-with-an-element-from-.title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
tries__maximum-xor-with-an-element-from-.pattern: Offline queries sorted by limit + incremental binary Trie
tries__maximum-xor-with-an-element-from-.statement: Given `nums` and queries `queries[i] = [xi, mi]`, for each query return the maximum `xi XOR nums[j]` over all `nums[j] <= mi`, or `-1` if no such element exists.

approaches.name: Sort queries by mi, add eligible numbers to a binary Trie
approaches.idea: Sort `nums` ascending and process queries in increasing order of the cap `mi`. Maintain a pointer that inserts numbers `<= mi` into a binary Trie, so the Trie always holds exactly the eligible candidates for the current query. Then answer each query with the same greedy opposite-bit walk as basic Maximum XOR; if nothing was inserted yet, the answer is `-1`.

tries__maximum-xor-with-an-element-from-.insight: The `<= mi` constraint becomes trivial if you answer queries offline in increasing mi, growing the Trie monotonically.

tries__concatenated-words.title: Concatenated Words
tries__concatenated-words.pattern: Trie of shorter words + word-break DP
tries__concatenated-words.statement: Given an array of distinct `words`, return all words that are concatenations of at least two words from the same array.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Sort by length, Trie of processed words, DP break
approaches.idea: Sort words by length so any concatenation is built only from strictly shorter words already inserted into a Trie. For each word run a word-break DP over the Trie: `dp[i]` means the prefix of length `i` is decomposable; extend from every reachable position by walking Trie edges and marking `dp[j+1]` at each word-terminal. Because building blocks are strictly shorter, reaching the end guarantees at least two pieces.
approaches.time: O(n log n + sum(L^2)) where L is word length

tries__concatenated-words.insight: Insert words shortest-first and break each against the Trie; if it splits at all, it splits into >= 2 pieces.

tries__palindrome-pairs.title: Palindrome Pairs
tries__palindrome-pairs.pattern: Hash map of words + palindrome split analysis
tries__palindrome-pairs.statement: Given a list of unique `words`, return all pairs of distinct indices `(i, j)` such that `words[i] + words[j]` is a palindrome.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Map lookup on palindromic splits
approaches.idea: Map each word to its index. For a word `w`, try every split `w = left + right`. If `left` is a palindrome and the reverse of `right` exists as another word `k`, then `k + w` is a palindrome (pair `[k, i]`). Symmetrically, if `right` is a palindrome and the reverse of `left` exists as word `k`, then `w + k` is a palindrome (pair `[i, k]`). Guarding the second case with `j != n` prevents counting the same pair twice while still handling empty strings.
approaches.time: O(n * k^2) where k is max word length

tries__palindrome-pairs.insight: Split each word; a palindromic half plus the reversed other half found in the map gives a pair (the reversed-suffix Trie is the O(n*k) alternative).

tries__stream-of-characters.title: Stream of Characters
tries__stream-of-characters.pattern: Trie of reversed words, match the stream backwards
tries__stream-of-characters.statement: Implement `StreamChecker(words)` and `query(letter)` that returns `true` if some word in `words` is a suffix of the characters queried so far.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters
1 <= letter is a lowercase English letter

approaches.name: Reversed-word Trie matched from newest char backward
approaches.idea: Insert each word reversed into a Trie. Keep the running stream; on each query walk the Trie from the most recent character backward, which matches word suffixes. Stop early once you pass `maxLen` characters or fall off the Trie, and return `true` as soon as a terminal node is reached.

tries__stream-of-characters.insight: Suffix matching becomes prefix matching if you store words reversed and read the stream backward.

tries__word-squares.title: Word Squares
tries__word-squares.statement: Given a list of unique `words` all of the same length, return all word squares that can be built. A sequence of words forms a word square if the k-th row and k-th column read the same string, for every k.

examples.explanation: Each row equals the corresponding column

constraints: All words[i] have the same length
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Trie prefix lookup with row-by-row backtracking
approaches.idea: Build a Trie where every node stores the indices of words passing through it, giving O(1)-ish prefix-to-candidates lookup. Fill the square row by row: when placing row `step`, the required prefix is the column formed by the already-placed rows' characters at position `step`. Query the Trie for words with that prefix, recurse, and backtrack. This prunes the search dramatically versus trying all word orderings.
approaches.time: O(n * 26^L * L) worst case, but prefix pruning makes it fast in practice

tries__word-squares.insight: Rows and columns must agree, so the next row's prefix is fixed by prior rows; a Trie turns that prefix into an instant candidate list.

tries__replace-words.title: Replace Words
tries__replace-words.pattern: Trie of roots, replace each word by its shortest root prefix
tries__replace-words.statement: Given a `dictionary` of root words and a `sentence`, replace every word in the sentence that has a root prefix in the dictionary with the shortest such root. Return the resulting sentence.

examples.input: dictionary = ["cat","bat","rat"], sentence = "the cattle was rattled by the battery"
examples.output: "the cat was rat by the bat"

constraints: sentence consists of lowercase letters and single spaces

approaches.name: Trie of roots, first terminal wins
approaches.idea: Insert all roots into a Trie. For each word in the sentence, walk the Trie character by character and return the prefix at the first terminal node encountered, which is by construction the shortest matching root. If the walk falls off the Trie, keep the original word.

tries__replace-words.insight: Walk each word down a Trie of roots and stop at the first word-end, which is automatically the shortest root.

tries__count-pairs-with-xor-in-a-range.title: Count Pairs With XOR in a Range
tries__count-pairs-with-xor-in-a-range.pattern: Binary Trie with subtree counts; count(<=high) - count(<low)
tries__count-pairs-with-xor-in-a-range.statement: Given `nums` and integers `low` and `high`, count pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` such that `low <= nums[i] XOR nums[j] <= high`.

approaches.name: Binary Trie with counts, reduce range to two prefix counts
approaches.idea: Answer = f(high+1) - f(low), where f(limit) counts pairs with XOR strictly less than limit. Process numbers left to right in a binary Trie whose nodes carry subtree counts; for each new number add (against already-inserted values) the count of partners giving XOR < high+1 minus those giving XOR < low, then insert it. To count partners with `num ^ v < limit`: at each bit, if the limit bit is 1, every partner keeping that XOR bit 0 is definitely smaller so add that whole subtree, then descend the branch that keeps the prefix tight; if the limit bit is 0, only the XOR-bit-0 branch can stay smaller, so descend there.

tries__count-pairs-with-xor-in-a-range.insight: Range XOR count = (pairs with XOR < high+1) - (pairs with XOR < low), and each is a single Trie descent using subtree counts.
